hook: Try to open a heavy door by pushing right next to the hinges: it barely moves. Push the same amount at the handle and it swings. Push straight at the hinges and nothing happens at all. How hard you push is only half the story; where and in which direction you push decide whether anything turns.

figure.caption: The lever arm is the perpendicular distance from the axis to the force’s line of action: r⊥ = r sin θ, and τ = r⊥F.

chain.cause: A force acts on an object that can turn about an axis
chain.effect: its line of action may pass the axis at some distance

chain.cause: The line of action misses the axis by a perpendicular distance r⊥
chain.effect: the force has a lever arm r⊥ = r sin θ

chain.cause: The force has a lever arm
chain.effect: it exerts a torque τ = r⊥F that tends to turn the object one way
their torques add with signs (counterclockwise +, clockwise −) to a net torque

chain.cause: A force’s line of action passes through the axis
chain.effect: its lever arm and its torque are zero

ideas: Torque is the turning effect of a force: τ = r⊥F = rF sin θ, in N·m.
The lever arm r⊥ is the perpendicular distance from the axis to the line of action, not the distance to the point where the force acts.
Only the part of a force perpendicular to r turns the object.
Give each torque a sign: counterclockwise + and clockwise − (or the reverse, stated). Add them for the net torque.
A force diagram starts each force at its point of application, labeled with type and agent.

misconception.wrong: The torque of a force is its size times the distance from the axis to where it acts, whatever its direction.
misconception.right: Only the perpendicular distance from the axis to the force’s line of action counts: τ = rF sin θ. A force along the line toward the axis has no torque however far out it acts.

summary: Torque measures how well a force turns an object about an axis: τ = r⊥F = rF sin θ, where the lever arm r⊥ is the perpendicular distance from the axis to the force’s line of action. Torques carry a sign for clockwise or counterclockwise and add to a net torque. A force diagram draws each force where it acts.
